audit_allocation.headline: Food service is over-represented: 52% of the money vs 28% of corridor businesses (1.8x). Likely cause: the applicant pool (the scenario's chosen applicants, not real demand).
memo_lines: Food service is over-represented: 52% of the money vs 28% of corridor businesses (1.8x). Likely cause: the applicant pool (the scenario's chosen applicants, not real demand).

Households without a car: 81% where the money lands (dollar-weighted) vs 74% corridor average, more car-free than average.
No sign of the edge generator's bias toward input-heavy industries in this plan.

caveats: Only 9 funded businesses: shares move a lot with one award. Read directions, not decimals.

The applicant queue is a scenario the team chose (sql/02_applications.sql) to include a hub, real cascades, one-hop food businesses and leaves. A skew traced to the applicant pool reflects that choice, not real demand.
Supply links are modeled from BEA industry rates, which favour input-heavy industries.
Tract location comes from business coordinates; demographics are ACS 2019 five-year estimates.
Race and ethnicity are not used anywhere, including this audit.
